topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, outlines the lecture scope on the initiation and resolution of inflammation, and frames how the concepts build on previously introduced immunology material.

topics.label: Innate Immune Recognition of Infection and Tissue Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system senses microbial threats and cellular injury using pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns detected by pattern recognition receptor families and the inflammasome.

topics.label: Inflammatory Cascade, Leukocyte Recruitment, and Systemic Effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how activated sentinel cells trigger leukocyte trafficking and extravasation to affected tissues and draining lymph nodes, as well as the life-threatening systemic risks of uncontrolled acute activation.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the active and passive mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, mediate tissue healing, and give rise to chronic inflammation and granuloma containment when insults persist.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation and announces the topic of the next lecture.
